chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Miskan, from Abi Basir, who said:

I asked him about a man who forgot the Zuhr prayer until the time of the 'Asr prayer entered. He said: “He begins with the prescribed prayer, and likewise with the prayers, you begin with the one that you forgot, unless you fear that the time of the prayer will go out; then you begin with the one whose time you are in, then you perform the qada' of the one you forgot.”

key_terms.الظُّهْرَ: the Zuhr salat (prayer), the noon prescribed prayer
key_terms.تَقْضِي: to perform as qada', making up a missed obligation
key_terms.يَخْرُجَ وَقْتُ الصَّلَاةِ: that the appointed time of the salat (prayer) expires

ai.seo_question: If someone forgets Zuhr until 'Asr time begins, which salat (prayer) should be performed first?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding one who forgets an earlier salat (prayer) until the time of a later salat (prayer) begins. The principle is to begin with the missed prayer first, unless there is fear that the current prayer's time will expire, in which case the current prayer is performed first and the forgotten one is made up afterward.
